findings.verdictRationale: Six of the seven targets are resolved or clearly improved compared with r5. The roof cross-band, the hatch-lid triangle and the left stripe end are effectively closed. The whole-vehicle read has not yet crossed into fire aftermath. At 256 and 128 the rear half reads mainly as a flat, uniform warm-dark brown livery or partial camouflage on an otherwise pristine tank, not as burned coating. The causes are visible: no tonal or scorch transition between charcoal and retained paint, a still-continuous tapered stripe on the right lower hull, and stair-stepped mask edges at 1000. These are bounded finishing problems, not a reason to redesign the direction or palette. The candidate should be corrected rather than kept as-is for final finishing.

targetFindings.target: 1 RightStowage outer face 2 / front return face 3
targetFindings.observation: In r5 1000-right, black fill ran across the lower bustle side under a jagged 'skyline' top. In r6 1000-right, char starts at the upper edge and wraps down. Irregular tan retained paint remains along the lower-left and middle, and the dark front return face now joins top and side as one dark mass. The skyline reading is gone. The boundary is still stepped, with blocky stair-step contours, and the tan islands keep sharp blotch shapes. At 1000 front-three-quarter, the left bustle face shows a similar tan-blotch-in-dark pattern that reads as desert camouflage. This is not just an inverted stencil, because the coverage proportion and the join to the return face changed. But the edge is the same hard binary contour, so it still reads as a mask edge rather than heat-softened paint loss.

targetFindings.target: 2 Long lower Hull-side stripe / rear right skirt P14
targetFindings.observation: In r6 1000-right the lower boundary varies more than r5's near-horizontal hard edge, and the rear skirt section is darker. The dark area is still one continuous wedge from the rear deck tapering forward to a point near mid-hull, following the upper hull slope. At 256-right and 128-right it still reads as one long dark sweep or racing stripe. I accept that the sloped side surface is physical. The issue is the continuous taper of the char mask over that surface, not the silhouette.

In r5 1000-top, a beige horizontal band crossed the bustle and turret roof between dark regions. In r6 1000-top, the roof from the grille deck to the turret-roof front edge is continuous dark. The bright rectangular panel rims remain as thin light outlines. I read them as physical highlight rims, not paint. They do read somewhat like clean trim lines, which is a mild cue conflict, but they are outside this target.

r5 1000-rear-three-quarter showed a beige triangle or wedge on the dark lid. In r6 the lid exterior is uniform dark with only a small light vertical mark, consistent with the retained small source detail 163 (latch or handle). The lid interior seen in 1000-front is dark grey, consistent with interior 32.

In r6 1000-rear-three-quarter, the rear plate around the three louver banks is now dark. In r5 that face was clean tan. A narrow tan lower apron band and a tan right end cap remain, with rectilinear borders that match part boundaries. Per the brief, I do not call these a missing map. They do read as a clean band under the char at 1000 and faintly at 256.

perViewScaleFindings.1000: Target fixes are legible. The main remaining cues are: (a) flat, uniform charcoal with no internal variation, (b) a hard binary edge between char and tan with no scorched, browned or blistered fringe, (c) visible stair-step aliasing on mask contours, clearest on the right bustle edge in top view, the right hull-side wedge, and the left-bustle blotches in front-three-quarter. The front hull, glacis, turret front and left hull side are fully pristine. In front-three-quarter that creates a 'rear half dipped in brown' read.
perViewScaleFindings.256: In rear-three-quarter, the rear deck and bustle read as a dark-brown painted section. In right view, the hull-side wedge reads as a stripe and the bustle as camouflage-like dark with tan patches. Front and left views read almost undamaged, with only the rear deck dark. Front occlusion legitimately limits cues there, so I do not require equal coverage.
perViewScaleFindings.128: Damage is legible only as a dark rear mass in right, rear-three-quarter and top views. Front, left and front-three-quarter read essentially as an intact tan tank with a dark engine deck. The silhouette stays recognisable as an Abrams. The condition reads as 'darkened rear' more than 'burned-out wreck'.

sourceComparison.referencesShowQualitatively: Hansen 2003 shows char and soot spread over most of the turret and hull side, with mottled lighter retained coating, pale ash-white heat-bleached patches, soft and fragmented boundaries, and a lot of tonal variation inside dark areas. Doha I14 shows large dark areas whose upper hull and skirt edges are ragged. Retained lighter paint has irregular, blistered boundaries, and the dark regions vary from grey to black-brown.
sourceComparison.candidateRelativeToReferences: r6 matches the qualitative idea of connected dark areas with irregular retained coating better than r5. It does not match the references' tonal range or edge softness. Its char is one flat warm brown-black value, and every boundary is a hard binary step. Both photos show irregular, multi-tone transitions. I make no claim about incident, heat direction, substrate or radiometry. This comparison is about visual morphology only.
sourceComparison.protectedOriginals: The pristine-looking steel louvers, dark rubber road wheels, grey weapons, antennas, glass blocks and tan trim (e.g., periscope housings, smoke launchers, the clean barrel) add to the 'intact vehicle' read, especially the clean tan barrel and front components. I note this as an effect on the overall condition, not as a binding defect.

remainingPhysicalVsMaskVsLightingUncerta: The dark rectangle on the right lower hull side, mid-length, appears in both r5 and r6. It matches the attributed existing Hull24 missing-skirt-backing placeholder. It reads as a flat dark hole. I treat it as physical/placeholder, not as the new field.
The front view's dark olive lower hull plate and black wheel area appear unchanged and look physical or material, not part of the new field. I am uncertain whether they are shading or base material.
The diagonal dark band across the front hull and glacis in 1000-front and 1000-front-three-quarter matches the gun barrel's cast shadow. It is lighting, not texture.
The thin dark lines across the top-view roof and the bustle shadows match antenna and rack cast shadows.
The thin light dashed line across the dark right hull wedge at about deck-edge height may be a physical seam or fender edge highlight, or a mask gap. Images alone cannot tell.

The tan lower rear apron and end-cap borders follow part edges. Whether they are unselected frame faces 60/61/128 or deliberate retained paint cannot be established from the images. I accept the attributed explanation.
No visibly blocking physical problem was observed. The silhouette, wheels, tracks and turret placement read coherently.

Use a darkened blend of each role's source paint toward the existing charcoal, plus a little low-amplitude value break-up inside large char areas.
